A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same cost-optimal GQA research. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support comparison despite substantial reorganization and changes to the title and authorship.

before.justification: v1 reports original language-model training results, including loss scaling, head-count and context-length analyses, and context-extension experiments in Section 4 and the appendices.

after.justification: v2 reports original scaling experiments and adds measured throughput, downstream accuracy, and retrieval results in Section 5.5 and Table 5.

M1.justification: v2 retains head/hidden-size decoupling and joint resource allocation but introduces a hardware-aware objective Z and a constrained search that selects configurations using inverted loss-scaling curves (Section 4.1). The reported model architecture also changes from explicitly ungated SiLU FFNs in v1 Appendix C to SwiGLU FFNs in v2 Appendix D.

E1.justification: SlimPajama language modeling remains, while v2 adds an eight-task downstream accuracy aggregate and RULER single-needle retrieval across contexts up to 128K (Section 5.5, Appendix J.2). These introduce reasoning and explicit information-retrieval requirements absent from v1's evaluations.

E2.justification: The appendix cost comparisons change comparator membership: v1 Figures 12–14 include standard size-scaled MHA and MQA, while v2 Figures 9–11 compare Llama-3 GQA with fixed head configurations and omit those two standard curves. MHA remains in the aligned-training-cost comparison, so it has not disappeared from the paper entirely.

E3.justification: The default training budget changes from 10B tokens per model to 20 tokens per parameter. Fixed d/L=128 configurations are replaced by a different model-size and aspect-ratio schedule, and v2 reports learning-rate selection by model size. New protocols introduce Z, downstream training with 20B tokens at 4K followed by 1B at 128K, and batch-one inference-throughput measurement on an A800. These are reported setting changes, not proof that every retained experiment was rerun.

E4.justification: The existing context-length sensitivity analysis is revised into relative-loss comparisons across GQA configurations and an explicit model-size comparison (v2 Figures 5–6). The fixed-KV-head analysis is also reworked with different fitted functions and configurations. The aligned-compute and 2K-to-64K post-training analyses already existed in v1; their retention or relocation is not a new robustness study.

E5.justification: v2 Appendix J.2 newly specifies averaging downstream scores over the last four checkpoints to reduce randomness. This is checkpoint aggregation, not four independent training runs. Neither version reports independent-seed uncertainty intervals or significance tests for these comparisons.

E6.justification: v2 adds optimal-configuration results in Table 4 and throughput/downstream results in Table 5, including inference throughput of 12,921 versus 20,643 tokens/s and common-sense accuracy of 45.7% versus 45.5%. Reported headline memory/FLOPs reductions change from 48.4%/49.6% to 50.8%/57.8%, under revised model and training settings rather than an unchanged comparison. The fixed-KV finding changes from a logarithmic fit with R2 above 0.99 to a power-plus-constant fit with R2 above 0.97. The aligned-compute 88%/83% reductions remain.

T1.justification: v2 adds a formal loss-constrained optimization objective, the composite cost definition Z, and a derivation of the minimum model size satisfying the target loss (Equations 5–9). Appendix I replaces v1's logarithmic fixed-KV scaling relation with a power-plus-constant relation and imposes a shared asymptote of 1.53 for the context-specific head-scaling fits. The basic inference and training cost identities are retained.

C1.justification: v1 primarily claims a systematic scaling study and improved resource allocation during training and inference. v2 makes an explicit three-step recipe for inference-cost-optimal GQA a central contribution and claims savings exceeding 50% without degradation in model capabilities. The central recommendation to combine fewer heads with larger models remains, while the attention-head scaling result moves to the appendix.

C2.justification: v2 replaces v1's rationale for excluding actual throughput with hardware-aware optimization and interpretation of measured throughput. It removes the specific approximately-20B crossover argument, adds limitations concerning extrapolation to larger models and training datasets, and separately expresses confidence up to 10B parameters. Appendix B also newly argues that the analysis applies to MLA, extending the stated applicability beyond v1's generic discussion of other attention mechanisms.

D1.justification: v2 adds search implementation details, aspect-ratio interpolation and binary search, learning-rate grids, training/evaluation precision, and downstream training and scoring instructions. These substantially expand reproducibility information beyond v1. Reporting inconsistencies remain: Table 7 appears to interchange d and L relative to Table 9, and the main-text FFN formulation is not reconciled with Appendix D's SwiGLU specification. The code link is retained, while v1's prospective code/data-release promise disappears.

R1.justification: The GQA, efficient-attention, and scaling-law literature framework remains. v2 adds citations for the evaluation harness, RULER, and Qwen3, removes the FlashAttention-2 and GELU citations, and expands discussion of applicability to MLA. Qwen2.5 remains the same cited work despite its changed author attribution.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction are substantially rewritten, terminology changes from parametric/non-parametric to time-invariant/time-variant costs, and separate Preliminaries and Method sections reorganize the narrative. Training-cost derivations, head-scaling analyses, discussions, and post-training material move into reorganized appendices. The title and author list also change.

P2.justification: v2 introduces a prominent explanatory schematic with cost bars, adds optimal-configuration and downstream-results tables, and expands cost plots with a third Z panel. Appendix comparison plots are consolidated, context analyses use new relative-loss axes, and head-scaling and post-training figures relocate to the appendices. These are substantial display and layout changes beyond numerical updates or renumbering.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially improves practical usability and empirical support. v1 relies on loss curves and analytical cost estimates; v2 supplies an actionable constrained search and tests a selected configuration with measured throughput and downstream outcomes (Section 4.1, Table 5). This addresses an important gap in the efficiency argument. Inconsistent model specifications and missing independent-run uncertainty still limit reproducibility and the strength of the no-degradation claim, but the added practical validation and explicit procedure provide substantial overall gains.
